---
title: "Setup"
subtitle: "What to install before the sessions"
number-sections: false
---

You need a working R + Quarto toolchain and an editor. Everything below is standard; if you
already render Quarto documents from R, you are ready.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## Setup at a glance
Four steps, top to bottom — each links to its details below:

1. [**Install**](#software) R ≥ 4.5, Quarto ≥ 1.9, and an editor.
2. [**Get the materials**](#get-the-materials) — one line of R, no git or GitHub account needed.
3. [**Install the R packages**](#r-packages) — one `install.packages()` line.
4. [**Check it works**](#check-your-setup) — `source("00-check-setup.R")` from the exercises folder.

Do steps 2–4 **before you arrive** — walking in with the toolchain already in place means we start on the content, not the install.
:::

## Software

- **R ≥ 4.5.0.** The running dataset (`penguins`) ships in base R only since 4.5 — check with
  `R.version.string`. The exercises use the base-R names (`bill_len`, `bill_dep`, …), so R ≥ 4.5
  is the smoothest path; if you truly can't upgrade, see the fallback below.
- **Quarto ≥ 1.9.** Check with `quarto --version`; get it from
  <https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/>. (1.9 is required — the Typst margin/article layout we
  use on Day 1 landed in 1.9.)
- **An editor with Quarto support** — [Positron](https://positron.posit.co/), VS Code (+ the
  Quarto extension), or RStudio. All work; we drive Quarto from the command line too
  (`quarto preview` / `quarto render`), so the editor is your choice.

::: {.callout-tip}
Typst (the modern PDF path we use on Day 1) ships **inside** Quarto — there is nothing extra to
install, no LaTeX.
:::

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true"}
## Stuck on R < 4.5? (dataset fallback)
The exercises assume base R's `penguins`. If you genuinely can't get to R ≥ 4.5, install
[`palmerpenguins`](https://allisonhorst.github.io/palmerpenguins/) and rename its columns to the
base-R names the material uses — then every snippet works unchanged:

```r
# install.packages("palmerpenguins")
library(dplyr)
penguins <- palmerpenguins::penguins |>
  rename(
    bill_len    = bill_length_mm,
    bill_dep    = bill_depth_mm,
    flipper_len = flipper_length_mm,
    body_mass   = body_mass_g
  )
```

Run this once at the top of a document (or your session) before the exercise code. Upgrading R is
still the cleaner path if you can.
:::

## Get the materials

The hands-on files live in a small **exercises folder** — the starter documents, the reference
solutions, and the citation assets (`references.bib`, `apa.csl`). The easiest way to get it — **no
git, no GitHub account, nothing to unzip by hand**, identical on Windows/macOS/Linux — is
**`use_course()`** from R:

```r
# install.packages("usethis")   # once, if you don't have it
usethis::use_course("cderv/raukr-quarto-exercises@raukr-2026")
```

**What it does**, so nothing surprises you:

1. picks a sensible spot — your **Desktop** by default — and prints where it's about to download. To
   put it elsewhere, cancel and re-run with a path, e.g.
   `use_course("cderv/raukr-quarto-exercises@raukr-2026", destdir = "~/projects")`.
2. downloads a ZIP, **unpacks it for you** into a folder called `raukr-quarto-exercises` (it prints
   the exact path), and asks *"Shall we delete the ZIP file?"* — say **No**, and keep it: it's your
   one-click reset (see below).
3. **opens the folder** — a new RStudio session, or (in Positron / VS Code) the folder; if it doesn't
   pop open, open the folder it printed yourself.

::: {.callout-important}
## Open the **day folder**, not the top folder
The exercises folder holds one self-contained folder per day. Open the one for the session — **not**
the top `raukr-quarto-exercises` folder:

- **Day 1** → open **`day1-intro/`** (double-click `day1-intro.Rproj`).
- **Day 2** → open **`day2-projects/`** (double-click `day2-projects.Rproj`).

Each day folder is its own working directory with its own brand and assets, so your renders land
**right next to your files** — there's no project folder above them to capture the output. One
download covers both days; the reference answers are in `solutions/` (try first).
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Reset without losing work (no git needed)
If an attempt goes sideways, get a **fresh** copy of the day folder — don't try to unzip over your
working copy:

- **re-run** `usethis::use_course("cderv/raukr-quarto-exercises@raukr-2026")` — it makes a new,
  numbered folder and leaves your old attempt untouched; **or**
- unzip the ZIP you kept to a **new** location.

If `use_course()` can't reach GitHub (venue firewall), use the browser: the green **Code ▸ Download
ZIP** button on <https://github.com/cderv/raukr-quarto-exercises/tree/raukr-2026>, then unzip.
:::

## R packages

The exercises use nine R packages. The simplest path — and the one that works no matter which day
folder you open — is a plain install into your R library:

```r
install.packages(c(
  "dplyr", "ggplot2", "gt", "ggokabeito",   # content + a colour-blind-safe scale
  "brand.yml", "ggrepel", "prismatic",      # R-side branding for the Typst payoff
  "knitr", "rmarkdown"                      # the engine every .qmd with R code needs
))
```

Or with [**pak**](https://pak.r-lib.org/) — same list, but it installs in parallel, prefers
binaries, and sorts out system dependencies for you:

```r
# install.packages("pak")   # once, if you don't have it
pak::pak(c(
  "dplyr", "ggplot2", "gt", "ggokabeito",
  "brand.yml", "ggrepel", "prismatic",
  "knitr", "rmarkdown"
))
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Prefer pinned versions? (optional, `renv`)
The exercises ship an `renv.lock` recording exact package versions. From the **top**
`raukr-quarto-exercises` folder (where `renv.lock` sits):

```r
# install.packages("renv")   # if you don't have it
renv::restore()
```

`renv` builds a **project-local** library at that top folder — handy for exact reproducibility, but
the plain `install.packages()` above is the simpler path when you open the day folders directly. Pick
one; you don't need both.
:::

## Check your setup

The exercises folder ships a one-shot check. From the **top** `raukr-quarto-exercises` folder, run:

```r
source("00-check-setup.R")
```

It verifies R ≥ 4.5, Quarto ≥ 1.9, the nine packages, and the base-R `penguins` data, then **renders
the Day-1 Typst sample** (`day1-intro/sample-typst.qmd`) — which proves the knitr + Typst chain
end-to-end and **caches the brand's Google fonts** (Albert Sans / Fira Mono), so your first render in
the session is instant instead of pausing to download them. Every line should read `[ok]`.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Prefer to check by hand?
The one command that proves the toolchain — including the **knitr engine** (the `knitr` + `rmarkdown`
packages a `.qmd` with R code needs) — is `quarto check`: it reports your Quarto version and renders a
small knitr test document (look for `Checking Knitr engine render......OK`). If you see
`rmarkdown: (None)`, your R packages aren't installed yet — do the [R packages](#r-packages) step and
re-run. Then confirm the R side:

```r
R.version.string                          # want >= 4.5.0
"penguins" %in% ls("package:datasets")    # want TRUE on R >= 4.5
```

And pre-warm the fonts once by rendering the sample yourself:
`quarto render day1-intro/sample-typst.qmd`.
:::
